typescript.description: Architectural directives, strict typing, and best practices for the modern TypeScript ecosystem.
architecturalRules: Modular architecture and decoupled components adhering to the Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)
DRY Principle: maximum reusability and zero logical duplication
Immutability by default: use readonly, immutable objects, and reactive Signals
Strict separation between presentation layer, business logic, and data access
qualityStandards: Strict typing enabled (strict: true) with zero tolerance for the any type
Zero tolerance for dead code, orphan imports, or unused variables
Automated unit and integration tests for critical business logic
typescript.gitConvention: Conventional Commits (feat, fix, refactor, style, test, chore)
typescript.customInstructions: Prioritize readability, composability, and rendering performance.

python.description: Development standards, Clean Architecture, and directives for backend services and AI applications in Python.
architecturalRules: Clean Architecture with decoupled layers (Domain, Application, Infrastructure)
Mandatory Type Hints across all functions and classes per PEP 484
Explicit error handling using custom domain exceptions
Idiomatic asynchronous programming using asyncio and dependency injection
qualityStandards: Strict validation with Ruff and Mypy in strict mode
Automated tests with Pytest, typed fixtures, and coverage above 80%
Google Style docstrings clearly documenting arguments and return types
python.gitConvention: Conventional Commits (feat, fix, refactor, test, chore)
python.customInstructions: Favor immutability using dataclasses(frozen=True) or Pydantic BaseModel(frozen=True).

go.description: Directives for idiomatic Go development, high concurrency, and resilient microservices.
architecturalRules: Small, decoupled interfaces defined at the consumption point (accept interfaces, return structs)
Explicit idiomatic error handling (if err != nil); never discard returned errors
Safe concurrency using goroutines, sync.WaitGroup, and channels with context control (context.Context)
Standard Go project layout (cmd/, internal/, pkg/)
qualityStandards: Zero data races: always verify with 'go test -race'
Unit and integration testing using standard testing package and table-driven tests
go.gitConvention: Conventional Commits (feat, fix, refactor, perf, chore)
go.customInstructions: Avoid unnecessary abstractions; favor clear, direct code with zero superfluous dependencies.

rust.description: Directives for memory-safe, high-performance, and idiomatic systems development in Rust.
architecturalRules: Strict adherence to ownership and borrowing rules without unnecessary defensive clones
Explicit, typed error handling using Result<T, E> and the '?' operator
Rich domain modeling with algebraic data types (Enums with payloads) and exhaustive pattern matching
Internal modularity with restricted crate visibility (pub(crate))
qualityStandards: Zero tolerance for 'unsafe' blocks without rigorous, documented justification
Clean compilation with zero warnings using 'cargo clippy -- -D warnings'
Unit, integration, and property-based tests using 'cargo test'
rust.gitConvention: Conventional Commits (feat, fix, refactor, perf, chore)
rust.customInstructions: Ensure errors contain descriptive contextual information before propagating.

java.role: Senior Enterprise Architect & Spring Boot Specialist
java.description: Directives for enterprise architecture, Domain-Driven Design (DDD), and clean code standards for Java & Spring Boot.
architecturalRules: Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters) isolating the core domain model
Strict constructor-based dependency injection; avoid field injection (@Autowired)
Immutability encouraged using Java Records and immutable DTOs
Global exception handling via @RestControllerAdvice and RFC 7807 ProblemDetails
qualityStandards: Adherence to Checkstyle standards and static analysis with SonarQube
Unit and integration testing with JUnit 5, AssertJ, Mockito, and Testcontainers
Declarative input validation using Jakarta Bean Validation (@Valid)
java.gitConvention: Conventional Commits (feat, fix, refactor, test, chore)
java.customInstructions: Follow SOLID principles rigorously and prevent framework coupling in the business layer.
